title: No charges to be laid in shooting by police: Man shot and killed in back hills pursuit
article: Charges will not be laid against the RCMP officer who shot and killed a Kamloops man after a pursuit into the back hills outside the city last summer.
The dead man's sister said Thursday her family will have to rely on a coroner's inquest to bring them justice.
"I haven't closed my mind or my heart to the hope that charges could still be laid. An inquest is the only hope of that," Claire Hanaghan said.
"I would like charges only because of the emotion that someone should be responsible for this."
Two days ago Claire learned charges will not be laid against the Kamloops RCMP officer who killed her brother, Stephen Mace Hanaghan, 45, last June.
The news came as a shock to her and other family members. She admitted her brother was no saint but believes the officer used excessive force when he drew his weapon and opened fire.
Stan Lowe, communications counsel for the province's Criminal Justice Branch, disagreed, saying a review by Crown counsel revealed the officer's actions were "necessary and reasonable."
"All the circumstances and evidence were researched. The investigation itself was very thorough," he said.
Hanaghan was shot moments after he backed a Chevy pickup into an RCMP Suburban on Noble Lake Road.
He and a 45-year-old passenger were pursued through Westsyde by police after witnesses spotted them breaking into a Super Save gas station on Westsyde Road.
Kamloops RCMP turned the investigation over to Kelowna RCMP's major crime unit. This review was forwarded to Victoria late last year.
Claire said there have been too many shootings like this in recent years. She referred to Ian Geoffrey Bush, 22, who was shot and killed by a Houston RCMP officer while in police custody.
"It seems like poor judgment is used again and again. It seems like incidents like this are growing and growing," she said.
As long as the RCMP is allowed to monitor itself deaths like this will go unanswered, she said.
Lowe said a detachment never investigates itself. Investigators from neighbouring detachments are brought in to keep the review impartial and unbiased.
Claire said an inquest date has not been set. She hopes it will be soon.
"This has been hard on the family. It's been a tough year," she said.
In the meantime she will remember her brother as a charismatic, outgoing father of three, and not the man he was before he died.
"He was a different person at the end," she said.
Court records show Hanaghan had been charged with theft under $5,000 twice during the last two years of his life.
